reasoning_traces.think:
The system begins with raw features from multiple models—Elo, Poisson, market, power, standings—each producing a probability estimate z_i. These are transformed into log-odds space via logit(z_i). Aggregator A applies regularized logistic regression to these logits, incorporating a decorrelation penalty to reduce redundancy among inputs. This produces an aggregated probability p_agg. Simultaneously, a hierarchical negative binomial model (Totals Model B) estimates total runs, accounting for team-specific variability through shared random effects. The final meta-model (C) combines logit(p_agg) and logit(p_tot) using logistic regression to produce a decorrelated, calibrated final probability p_final. The final distributional layer (D) applies IDR or multicalibration to ensure that predicted probabilities align with empirical frequencies, forming a robust, calibrated probabilistic output. Failure modes include overfitting in aggregation, mis-specification in the totals model, and collinearity in the meta-model.
